objectives: Explain why attention needs position information
Compare sinusoidal vs learned vs rotary encodings

slides.title: Part 1 — Why position has to be injected
slides.body: Self-attention is powerful but has one blind spot you must patch.

slides.title: Attention is permutation-equivariant
slides.body: Self-attention is a *set* operation: shuffle the input tokens and the outputs shuffle identically — the math contains no notion of "first" or "after". But language is ordered: "dog bites man" ≠ "man bites dog". Position information is **not** in the mechanism; it must be added to the token representations explicitly.

slides.title: The fix: add a position-dependent vector
slides.body: Before the first attention layer, add a vector $PE(pos)$ to each token embedding. Now two copies of the same word at different positions have different representations, so attention *can* condition on order. The design question is only: what should $PE(pos)$ be?

slides.title: Sinusoidal — the original recipe
slides.body: $PE_{(pos,2i)}=\sin\!\big(pos/10000^{2i/d}\big)$, odd indices use $\cos$. Low dimensions oscillate fast (encode fine/local position), high dimensions slowly (coarse/global position). Geometric wavelengths give every position a unique fingerprint *and* make relative offsets expressible as a linear function — watch the wavelength grow with the dimension index:

question.explanation: Low dims oscillate fast (local position), high dims slowly (global position) — together a unique, relative-offset-friendly code.

question.question: Why does attention need positional encoding at all?
options: Attention is permutation-invariant — it sees every token pair but not their order
Attention cannot compute dot products without it
It is required for softmax to converge
question.explanation: Attention treats the input as a set: permuting inputs permutes outputs but doesn't change the computation. Order has to be injected into the inputs (added vectors) or into Q/K (RoPE) so the model can reason about sequence.

slides.title: Rotate, don't add
slides.body: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) **rotates** the Q and K vectors by an angle proportional to position instead of adding a vector. The dot product $Q_i\cdot K_j$ then depends only on the *relative* offset $i-j$ — relative position falls out of the algebra for free, and it extrapolates to longer contexts far better than learned absolute tables.

slides.title: Why relative position is the right inductive bias
slides.body: "The adjective modifies the next noun" is a *relative* rule — it shouldn't matter whether it happens at position 5 or 5000. Schemes that bake in relative offsets (RoPE, ALiBi) generalize across lengths; absolute learned embeddings overfit to positions seen in training and break past the trained context window.

question.question: The main practical advantage of RoPE over learned absolute positional embeddings is:
options: It encodes RELATIVE position into Q·K and extrapolates to longer contexts than seen at training
It uses fewer parameters and is faster
It removes the need to train the model
question.explanation: Learned absolute embeddings memorize only the positions seen in training — position 8000 is undefined if you trained to 4000. RoPE's rotation is parametric in position and shows up as a relative offset in the dot product, so it generalizes far better to long context.

slides.title: Part 4 — Ablate it & watch it break (pitfalls)
No PE → order-blind model
slides.body: Remove positional encoding entirely and the model still does *okay* on order-agnostic tasks (topic/bag-of-words) but fails completely on anything order-sensitive ("is X before Y?", subject vs object). The selective nature of the failure is the tell.

question.question: Order these positional schemes from OLDEST to NEWEST as the dominant default in transformer LLMs.
question.explanation: Sinusoidal came with the original 2017 transformer; learned absolute embeddings dominated the BERT/GPT-2 era; RoPE is the current default for modern LLMs because of its relative-position structure and extrapolation. (ALiBi is another modern relative-bias alternative.)

question.question: Diagnose the selective failure.
question.scenario: With positional encoding removed, the model still does okay on topic classification but fails completely on 'is token X before token Y?' style tasks.

rubricCriteria.description: order-dependent tasks fail because position is invisible to the model

question.explanation: No PE ⇒ permuting inputs permutes outputs identically. Bag-of-words-ish tasks tolerate that; anything order-sensitive collapses.

hints: Attention treats input as a set.
slides.workedSolution: Without PE the network is permutation-equivariant — order-blind. Topic/bag-of-words tasks don't need order; 'before/after' relations are impossible.

question.question: Remove positional encoding entirely. Which degrades MOST?
question.explanation: Attention is a set operation; with no PE the model literally cannot tell token order, so order-dependent tasks fail while order-agnostic ones survive.

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body: Attention is order-blind; position is injected (added sinusoids, or rotated in via RoPE — the modern default for its relative-offset bias). Next: the per-token compute engine — **[the FFN](/paths/ml-engineer/lessons/ffn)**.
